opportunities.title: The MEV Bot Ate the Hacker: How $7.7M in Stolen rsETH Got Re-Stolen in One Block
opportunities.why_now: A live exploit was intercepted by a rival MEV bot within the same block, and Kelp then froze the address — a rare three-way security drama playing out on-chain right now.
opportunities.angle: Blow-by-blow security breakdown of the exploit-vs-MEV-bot race, framed as 'there is no honor among thieves' — end with what this means for anyone still trusting mempool privacy.

opportunities.title: Balancer Isn't Dying From the Hack — It's Dying From What Came After
opportunities.why_now: Balancer is reportedly considering a wind-down after restructuring failed to revive revenue, months after its exploit, proving the hack was the beginning of the end, not the end.
opportunities.angle: Post-mortem timeline piece: hack date vs. TVL/revenue decay vs. wind-down news, making the case that 'recovery theater' rarely works once trust is gone.

opportunities.title: CoinEx Just Became Exhibit #47 in Why 'Nine Years Old' Means Nothing
opportunities.why_now: CoinEx is shutting down after nine years in business, giving users a hard December deadline to withdraw — another reminder that exchange age is not a security guarantee.
opportunities.angle: Listicle/thread: 'exchanges that looked permanent and weren't,' with a blunt reminder to self-custody before the deadline, in the channel's fatalistic voice.

opportunities.title: Two Robinhood Engineers Allegedly Front-Ran Their Own Listings on Hyperliquid — This Is What Insider Trading Looks Like Onchain
opportunities.why_now: DOJ just charged two former Robinhood engineers with using inside knowledge of upcoming listings to trade Hyperliquid perpetuals ahead of the public.
opportunities.angle: Security/market-structure explainer: how 'transparent' onchain markets still get gamed by information asymmetry, and why perp DEXs are the new insider-trading playground.

opportunities.title: $570M Liquidated in a Day Because a Bill Failed a Procedural Vote — Congratulations, It Was Never Priced In
opportunities.why_now: Clarity Act's Senate defeat triggered $450M in ETF outflows and $570M in long liquidations within 24 hours, exposing how fragile 'regulatory clarity' pricing really was.
opportunities.angle: Markets-meets-security piece: dissect the leverage cascade as a structural risk story, not a political one — the real lesson is about overexposed longs, not Washington.
